title: AI Can't Replace Real Research in Empathy Mapping
partialText: AI can help you organize research you’ve already collected, but it can’t create research evidence about the specific, messy experience of real users.

title: The Custodial Era of UX: Cleaning Up After AI
partialText: AI lets teams build faster than UX can evaluate. UX can adapt by building shared judgment, accelerating evaluation, and guiding AI-generated designs.

title: Artificial Intelligence: Glossary
partialText: Plain-language definitions of the AI terms that come up in product and design work, from tokens and context windows to agents, evals, and prompt injection.

title: AI-Generated Images Can Perform as Well as Stock Photography
partialText: When users didn’t know whether an image was AI-generated, the images we tested did not create any perception penalty compared to stock photos.

title: Psychological Ownership: Own the Right Things
partialText: Psychological ownership can make you more effective, but you’ll struggle if it attaches to things you can’t control. Spot misplaced ownership and redirect it.

title: One AI Output Is an Example, Not an Evaluation
partialText: One output cannot establish how well an AI system performs. Evaluate with multiple representative inputs, repeated runs, and confidence intervals.

title: How to Decide When an AI Tool Is Worth Keeping
partialText: Pressure to adopt AI isn't evidence that a tool helps. The PROVE framework tests one tool against one task and produces a provisional decision you can defend.

title: Dogfooding vs. QA vs. User Research
partialText: Dogfooding, or using your own products internally, helps catch bugs, but it can't replace user research: your team knows too much to represent real users.

title: No New Name Has Replaced “UX”
partialText: A survey of 604 tech and design professionals found that “UX” remains the default name for our field, while alternative names remain fragmented.

title: Why You Need Mentorship and How to Get It Right
partialText: Mentorship is an essential growth tool that offers substantial personal and career benefits, but only if you engage in it properly.

title: A Concrete Definition of “Product Sense” (and How to Build It)
partialText: Product sense means predicting which product decisions will succeed based on patterns learned through experimentation — and knowing when those patterns apply.

title: UX-Context Design: Using UX Knowledge to Inform AI-Generated Design
partialText: As more interface work is AI-generated, the output of research and design shifts from documents written for humans to curated context that guides AI.

title: Don’t Outsource the Learning: Why Human-Led Research Still Matters in the Age of AI
partialText: Even if AI matches researcher-output quality, human-led research will remain essential — the team learning from observing users can't be outsourced.

title: Does Your Form Really Need a Dropdown List?
partialText: Dropdown lists can be used in narrow, specific scenarios, but misuse can cause more harm than alternatives.
